summary: Concentrated: 50 holdings, but the top ten are 79% of the portfolio.
Trades moderately: about 36% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for at least 7.4 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are cheaper, more profitable and smaller.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 3 of 9 full years.

profile.background: University of Colorado. A portfolio manager at UMB Investment Advisors before becoming president and chief investment officer of Semper Augustus Investments Group in 1998. Known for long annual letters, including detailed analysis of Berkshire Hathaway.
profile.approach: Concentrated holdings in quality businesses bought at prices that leave a margin of safety.

name: Chris Bloomstran
